candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: support evidence-based infection management and practices that reduce avoidable antimicrobial exposure and infection-related risk.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — antimicrobial de-escalation
candidate.educational_objective: When microbiology identifies a susceptible pathogen in sepsis, support antimicrobial de-escalation by discontinuing unnecessary agents or narrowing therapy rather than continuing avoidable broad empiric coverage.

options.A: Discontinue unnecessary agents or narrow the regimen to therapy directed at the identified susceptible pathogen.
options.B: Continue every empiric antimicrobial for the full course even when culture data show that several agents are unnecessary.
options.C: Broaden therapy further after susceptibility results identify a narrower active option.
options.D: Ignore microbiology results because de-escalation is recommended only when cultures remain negative.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommends antimicrobial de-escalation when a confirmed microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available. The guideline defines de-escalation as discontinuing unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or narrowing the spectrum when appropriate. B and C do the opposite of de-escalation. D is incorrect because the strongest de-escalation recommendation specifically applies when microbiologic diagnosis and susceptibility are available; the guideline also separately suggests de-escalation in selected culture-negative cases.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current adult sepsis guidance recommends antimicrobial de-escalation after microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility data, using discontinuation of unnecessary agents or spectrum narrowing as appropriate.
candidate.source_document_title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
candidate.source_locator: Antimicrobial Therapy recommendation: for adults with sepsis or septic shock, recommend de-escalation over no de-escalation when a confirmed microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available. Remarks: de-escalation involves discontinuing unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or narrowing antimicrobial spectrum where appropriate. Separate conditional recommendation supports de-escalation even when no pathogens are identified on final cultures.
candidate.source_organization: Society of Critical Care Medicine / European Society of Intensive Care Medicine, Surviving Sepsis Campaign
candidate.stem: An adult with sepsis initially receives broad empiric antimicrobial therapy. Culture and susceptibility results later identify one susceptible bacterial pathogen. Which change best reflects current antimicrobial de-escalation guidance?
